spans.s:
Laba, ‘quail’ (Perdix chinensis) is one of the victims at the
Aśvamedha (‘horse sacrifice’) in the Yajurveda.^1
1) Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 14, 5;
Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 24. Cf.
Nirukta, vii. 2, where Rv. x. 119 is
called the Labasūkta; the Anukramaṇī
(Index), too, gives Aindra Laba as the
author of that hymn. Cf. Bṛhaddevatā,
viii. 40, with Macdonell's note. Cf.
Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 90.
